questions.stem: The function f(x) = 2x² − 12x + 23 is rewritten in vertex form. Which expression is equivalent?
questions.why: Complete the square: 2(x² − 6x) + 23 = 2(x − 3)² − 18 + 23, so the vertex form is 2(x − 3)² + 5 with vertex (3, 5).

questions.stem: Which values solve x² + 6x + 13 = 0 over the complex numbers?
questions.why: The discriminant is 36 − 52 = −16, so x = (−6 ± 4i)/2 = −3 ± 2i.

questions.stem: For f(x) = (x − 2)³(x + 1)², what happens at each x-intercept of the graph?
options: The graph touches at x = 2 and crosses at x = −1.
The graph touches the axis at both intercepts.
The graph crosses the axis at x = 2 and touches it without crossing at x = −1.
The graph crosses the axis at both intercepts.
questions.why: An odd multiplicity makes the graph cross at x = 2, while an even multiplicity makes it touch and turn at x = −1.

questions.stem: What is the remainder when p(x) = 2x³ − 5x² + 4x − 7 is divided by x − 2?
questions.why: By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is p(2) = 16 − 20 + 8 − 7 = −3.

questions.stem: According to the Rational Root Theorem, which list gives all possible rational roots of 3x³ − 4x² + 5x − 6 = 0?
questions.why: Possible roots are factors of the constant 6 over factors of the leading coefficient 3: ±1, ±2, ±3, ±6, ±1/3, ±2/3.

questions.stem: Which expression is equal to (3 − 2i)(4 + 5i)?
Solve x² − 4x − 1 = 0 by completing the square. Which values of x are correct?
questions.why: Add 1 to both sides and complete the square: (x − 2)² = 5, so x = 2 ± √5.

questions.stem: The line y = 2x + 3 intersects the parabola y = x² − 2x + 3. What are the intersection points?
questions.why: Set x² − 2x + 3 = 2x + 3, giving x² − 4x = 0, so x = 0 or x = 4 and the points are (0, 3) and (4, 11).

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to (8x⁶)^(2/3) for x > 0?
questions.why: Raise each factor to 2/3: 8^(2/3) = 4 and (x⁶)^(2/3) = x⁴, so the result is 4x⁴.

questions.stem: What is the solution set of √(2x + 7) = x + 2?
questions.why: Squaring gives x² + 2x − 3 = 0, so x = 1 or x = −3; the second makes the right side negative, so only x = 1 works.

questions.stem: If f(x) = (x − 3)/5, which function is f⁻¹(x)?
questions.why: Swap x and y and solve: x = (y − 3)/5 gives y = 5x + 3.

questions.stem: For f(x) = x² + 1 and g(x) = 2x − 3, which expression equals (f ∘ g)(x)?
Which value equals ln(e⁷) + ln(e³)?
questions.why: Adding logs multiplies the arguments: ln(e⁷ · e³) = ln(e¹⁰) = 10.

questions.stem: Solve 3^(2x − 1) = 27^(x − 2) for x.
questions.why: Since 27 = 3³, the exponents are equal: 2x − 1 = 3x − 6, so x = 5.

questions.stem: Which expression gives the value of $4,000 invested for 6 years at 5% annual interest compounded quarterly?
questions.why: Quarterly compounding uses rate 0.05/4 per period and 4 · 6 = 24 periods, giving 4000(1 + 0.0125)²⁴.

questions.stem: An 80 mg sample of a substance has a half-life of 12 years. About how much remains after 30 years?
Solve log₃(x − 2) + log₃(x + 4) = 3.
questions.why: Combining logs gives (x − 2)(x + 4) = 27, so x² + 2x − 35 = 0 and x = 5 or x = −7; x = −7 is rejected because it makes both arguments negative.

questions.stem: For f(x) = (2x² − 8)/(x² − 3x + 2), which statement describes its asymptotes and holes?
options: Vertical asymptotes x = 1 and x = 2, horizontal asymptote y = 2
Vertical asymptote x = 1, hole at x = 2, horizontal asymptote y = 2
Vertical asymptote x = 2, hole at x = 1, horizontal asymptote y = 0
Hole at x = 1, vertical asymptote x = 2, no horizontal asymptote
questions.why: Factoring gives 2(x − 2)(x + 2)/((x − 1)(x − 2)); the shared factor x − 2 is a hole, x = 1 stays a vertical asymptote, and equal degrees give y = 2.

questions.stem: In an arithmetic sequence, a₃ = 11 and a₉ = 35. What is a₂₀?
questions.why: The common difference is (35 − 11)/6 = 4, so a₁ = 3 and a₂₀ = 3 + 19(4) = 79.

questions.stem: What is the sum of the infinite geometric series 6 + 4 + 8/3 + 16/9 + ⋯?
questions.why: The ratio is 2/3, so the sum is a/(1 − r) = 6/(1/3) = 18.

questions.stem: A geometric sequence has a₂ = 6 and a₅ = 48. What is a₈?
questions.why: The ratio satisfies r³ = 48/6 = 8, so r = 2; then a₈ = a₅ · r³ = 48 · 8 = 384.

questions.stem: What is the coefficient of x³ in the expansion of (2x − 3)⁵?
questions.why: The x³ term is C(5,3)(2x)³(−3)² = 10 · 8x³ · 9 = 720x³.

questions.stem: If θ = 5π/6, what is tan θ?
What are the amplitude and period of y = 3 sin(2x − π/2)?
questions.why: The amplitude is |3| = 3 and the period is 2π/2 = π; the −π/2 inside shifts the graph but changes neither.

questions.stem: A triangle has sides of length 7 and 10 with an included angle of 60°. What is the length of the third side?
questions.why: By the Law of Cosines, c² = 49 + 100 − 2(7)(10)cos 60° = 149 − 70 = 79, so c = √79.

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to (1 − cos²θ)/(sin θ cos θ) for values where it is defined?
questions.why: Since 1 − cos²θ = sin²θ, the expression becomes sin²θ/(sin θ cos θ) = sin θ/cos θ = tan θ.

questions.stem: Scores on a test are normally distributed with mean 70 and standard deviation 8. Approximately what percent of scores are above 86?
questions.why: A score of 86 is z = (86 − 70)/8 = 2; about 95% lie within two standard deviations, leaving about 2.5% in the upper tail.

questions.stem: How many distinct arrangements can be made from all the letters of the word BANANA?
questions.why: There are 6!/(3!·2!) = 720/12 = 60 arrangements because A repeats three times and N twice.

questions.stem: For events A and B, P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4, and P(A ∩ B) = 0.2. What is P(A | B)?
questions.why: P(A | B) = P(A ∩ B)/P(B) = 0.2/0.4 = 0.5, which also matches P(A), so the events are independent.

questions.stem: What is the domain of f(x) = √(x − 3)/(x − 5)?
questions.why: The radicand requires x ≥ 3 and the denominator excludes x = 5, so the domain is [3, 5) ∪ (5, ∞).

questions.stem: How is the graph of g(x) = −f(x + 2) − 1 obtained from the graph of f?
options: Reflect across the y-axis, shift 2 right, then shift 1 down
Reflect across the x-axis, shift 2 right, then shift 1 up
Reflect across the x-axis, shift 2 left, then shift 1 down
Reflect across the x-axis, shift 2 left, then shift 1 up
questions.why: The negative sign reflects over the x-axis, x + 2 shifts left 2, and −1 outside shifts the graph down 1.

questions.stem: The height in feet of a ball is h(t) = −16t² + 64t + 5, where t is time in seconds. What is the ball's maximum height?
questions.why: The vertex occurs at t = −64/(2·−16) = 2, and h(2) = −64 + 128 + 5 = 69 feet.

questions.stem: What is the solution set of x² − x − 6 ≤ 0?
questions.why: The parabola opens upward with zeros at x = −2 and x = 3, so it is at or below zero between them: −2 ≤ x ≤ 3.
